# A global extraction budget forces a quantitative interval-width defect

This note derives a necessary inequality for a proposed GLOBAL maximum
half-depth extraction mass in n=d=1. It strengthens the raw reflection
correlation average by using the endpoints and slopes of the actual
reflection profile. A concrete convex family shows that these inequalities
alone still do not exclude a below-half proposed budget.

Let C have positive interval fibers I_i=[l_i,r_i], indexed consecutively
by0,...,N-1. Set w_i=r_i-l_i, M=sum w_i. Let m be the global maximum
mass of a convex extraction with true integer centroid and local
half-depth. By the proved interval rigidity/extraction equivalence,

    m=max_(j,y) R_j(y),
    R_j(y)=sum_i |I_i intersect (2y-I_(2j-i))|.

For each j define

    K_j=min(j,N-1-j),  N_j=2K_j+1,
    C_j=sum_(i:0<=2j-i<N) w_i w_(2j-i),
    Delta_j=N_j w_j^2-C_j.                          (1)

## 1. Endpoint, slope, and correlation constraints of one actual profile

Convex compatibility puts every midpoint interval
(I_(j-k)+I_(j+k))/2 inside I_j. Hence

    R_j(l_j)=R_j(r_j)=0.

Each ORDERED overlap term, as a function of y, is a translated trapezoid
with slopes in [-2,2]. There are N_j such terms, so R_j is nonnegative,
continuous, piecewise affine, and 2N_j-Lipschitz. This includes coincident
knots without a differentiability assumption.

The exact correlation integral, including its Jacobian, is

    integral_(I_j) R_j(y) dy = C_j/2.               (2)

For one ordered pair, substitution s=2y gives one half of the integral
of the convolution of the two interval indicators, namely w_i w_(2j-i)/2.
The full support in y lies inside I_j by compatibility, so no term is
lost by the restricted integral.

Since R_j<=m globally, the preceding endpoint and Lipschitz information
gives the POINTWISE upper envelope

    R_j(l_j+x)<=min(m,2N_j x,2N_j(w_j-x)),
           0<=x<=w_j.                              (3)

Integrating that triangle clipped at height m proves

    C_j <= N_j w_j^2-(N_j w_j-m)_+^2/N_j.           (4)

This formula remains valid when m>=N_j w_j, in which case the proposed
height bound is inactive and the positive part vanishes. Omitting that
positive part would produce a false global summation at edge fibers.
Equivalently,

    (N_j w_j-m)_+^2<=N_j Delta_j,
    m>=N_j w_j-sqrt(N_j Delta_j).                   (5)

The second lower bound strictly improves the direct mean bound
C_j/(2w_j), since rationalizing its right side gives

    N_j C_j/[N_j w_j+sqrt(N_j Delta_j)]
       >=C_j/(2w_j),

with strict inequality here because C_j>0.

## 2. Exact curvature/asymmetry interpretation

Concavity of the width sequence gives
w_j>=(w_(j-k)+w_(j+k))/2. Put s_k=(w_(j-k)+w_(j+k))/2. Then

    Delta_j
      =2 sum_(k=1)^Kj [w_j^2-w_(j-k)w_(j+k)]
      =2 sum_k (w_j-s_k)(w_j+s_k)
          +(1/2)sum_k (w_(j-k)-w_(j+k))^2.         (6)

Every displayed summand is nonnegative. Thus a hypothetical below-half
maximum, m<M/2, imposes the explicit budget-sensitive conditions

    Delta_j >= (N_j w_j-M/2)_+^2/N_j               (7)

for every j, with strict inequality whenever N_j w_j>M/2. More precisely
one may keep any proposed budget b<M/2 in place of m in (5). A failure
of even ONE resulting inequality certifies a larger actual reflection
extraction, without assuming any sign of an affine contact multiplier.
For a constant width sequence, Delta_j=0 and (5) recovers the complete
retention of all N_j paired fibers at a central index.

The inequality retains an actual global mass budget together with the
full paired-width correlation and the allowable slopes of its reflection
profile. It does not replace the source by a continuous base integral.

## 3. Exact limitation of this budget test

Use the actual convex body with interval fibers

    [0,2], [0,6], [0,10], [0,3],

so M=21. The exact quantities in (1) are

    N_j=(1,3,3,1),
    C_j=(4,76,136,9),
    Delta_j=(0,32,164,0).

The STRICTLY BELOW-HALF proposed budget b=10 satisfies EVERY inequality
(5): the only nonzero left sides are

    (18-10)^2=64<=3*32=96,
    (30-10)^2=400<=3*164=492.

It also respects the elementary bound b>=max w_i. Thus the profile
endpoint/slope/correlation constraints alone do not contradict a
below-half budget, even for width data from one actual convex body.

The ACTUAL optimum for this body is12, not10, as proved in
`candidate 1176a6cc970482b9`.
The newer optimized-triple plateau inequality in
`candidate c412d1154d2768ef` also
forces12 directly at base2. There is no actual below-half extraction
counterexample here. The example instead shows exactly which data are
missing from (5): the compatible placement and plateau interaction of
the individual overlap terms, beyond their sum's area and slope bound.

This separates a proved budget-sensitive invariant from the still
unproved general retained-mass inequality.
